translations.text: First Act. Further, the acts of Judas Thomas the apostle, when he sold him to Habban the merchant so that he might go down and make disciples in India.
At that time all the apostles were in Jerusalem: Simon Peter and Andrew, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the tax collector,
and James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James. They divided the countries among themselves, so that each one of them
would preach in the region allotted to him and in the country to which his Lord sent him. By lot and division, India fell to Judas Thomas the apostle.
He did not want to go, saying, “I cannot find the strength for this, because I am weak, and I am a Hebrew.
How can I teach the Indians?” While Judas was thinking these things, our Lord appeared to him in a vision at night and said to him, “Do not be afraid, Thomas,
because my grace is with you.” But he would not be persuaded at all, saying, “Send me wherever you wish, our Lord. Only I will not go to India.”
While Judas was thinking these things, an Indian merchant happened to be in the southern region, from [?]. His name was Habban, and he had been sent by King Gondophares
to bring him a skilled carpenter. Our Lord saw him walking along the road and said to him, “Are you looking to buy a carpenter?”
He said to him, “Yes.” Our Lord said to him, “I have a slave who is a carpenter, whom I will sell to you.” And he pointed Thomas out to him from a distance.
He agreed with him on a price of twenty pieces of silver, and they wrote a deed as follows: “I, Jesus, son of Joseph the carpenter, from Bethlehem, a village in Judea,
acknowledge that I have sold Judas Thomas, my slave, to Habban, the merchant of King Gondophares.” When they had completed his documents,
Jesus took Judas and went to Habban the merchant. Habban saw him and said to him, “Is this your master?”
Judas said to him, “Yes, he is my master.” “Is this your master?” Habban the merchant said to him. “He has indeed sold you to me.” And Judas remained silent.
In the morning he got up and prayed. He pleaded with his Lord and said to him, “Here I am, our Lord. As you wish, let your will be done.” And he went to Habban the merchant,
taking nothing with him except the money paid for him, for our Lord had given it to him [?]. Judas went and found Habban the merchant
loading his belongings onto the ship, and he began to board with him. When they had boarded and sat down, Habban the merchant said to Judas,
“What craft are you skilled at practicing?” Judas said to him, “Carpentry and building—the work of a carpenter.”
Habban the merchant said to him, “What do you know how to make from wood, and what from stone?” Judas said to him, “From wood I have learned to make
plows, yokes, goads, pulleys for ferries, and oars for ships; and from stone, funerary monuments and tombs,
temples, and fortresses for kings.” Habban the merchant said to him, “That is precisely the kind of craftsman I was looking for.”
They began to sail, because the wind had risen. They sailed gently until they reached the port of Sandaruk.
When they disembarked and were making their way into the city, they heard, and Judas began asking,
“What is this celebration in this city?” They said to him, “The gods have brought you too to enjoy yourself in this city.
For the king has an only daughter, and he is giving her in marriage. This sound of rejoicing is from her wedding feast.”
The king had also sent out heralds to proclaim that everyone should come to the banquet.
The poor and the rich, slaves and free people, foreigners and townspeople alike were invited. Anyone who did not come to the banquet would be liable to punishment from the king.
Habban the merchant said to Judas, “Let us go too, so that we do not get a bad reputation, especially since we are strangers.”
After they had lodged at the inn and rested a little, they went to recline at the meal. Judas reclined in the middle.
They were all looking at him as a stranger who had come from another place. Habban the merchant, his master, was reclining elsewhere.
While they ate and drank, Judas tasted nothing at all. Those beside him said to him, “Why did you come here,
when you cannot eat or drink?” Judas said to them, “I came here for something more important than food and drink,
and also to please the king and fulfill his wish, because the heralds were announcing that anyone who heard and did not come would receive punishment.”
While they were eating and drinking, oil and bowls were also brought in for them, and they took them. Some anointed their faces,
some their beards, and some other parts of their bodies. But Judas was praising God and making the sign on the middle of his head.
He moistened his nostrils a little and put some on his ears, while lifting up his heart. A wreath of myrtle was placed on his head,
and he held a reed leaf in his hand. Then the female singer who was among the reclining guests went around to them all.
When she reached Judas, she stood over him and sang. This singer was a Hebrew woman.
Although she stood over him for a long time, Judas did not lift his face but kept looking at the ground. Then one of the cupbearers came,
raised his hand, and struck him on the cheek. Judas looked at him and said, “May my God forgive you for this in the world to come.
But in this world he will show his wonders through that hand which struck me, and I shall see a dog dragging it away.”
Then Judas began to sing this song: “Prepare yourself, daughter of light. She has the splendor of kings. Her appearance is majestic and desirable.
She is beautiful and adorned with every good deed. Her garments resemble flowers whose fragrance spreads sweetly. The king dwells upon her head and nourishes those who dwell with him below.
Truth is placed upon her head; joy dances at her feet. Her mouth is open, and it becomes her, for with it she speaks every praise.
The Son’s twelve apostles and the seventy-two thunder within her. Her tongue is the curtain of the doorway, which the priest lifts as he enters.
Her neck rises in steps, built by the first architect. Both her hands proclaim the land of life.
Her ten fingers open the gate of heaven. Her bridal chamber is radiant and filled with the fragrance of salvation. A censer is prepared within her.
Love, faith, and hope spread fragrance for everyone. Truth rests within. Her gates are adorned with truth. Her wedding attendants surround her,
all those whom she invited. Her holy bridesmaids speak praise before her. The living minister before her,
and await the coming of their bridegroom. They will shine in his glory and be with him in the kingdom that will never pass away, forever and ever.”
And all the righteous will be gathered in his glory. They will enter his delight one by one, and they will put on garments of light.
They will wrap themselves in the glory of their Lord and praise the living Father, whose majestic light they have received, and they will shine with their Lord’s radiance.
They have received from his provision, which never runs out, and have drunk of the life that makes those who drink it long and thirst for more.
And praise the Father, the Lord of all, and the only Son who comes from him, and give thanks to the Spirit, his wisdom. While he was singing this song,
all those beside him were looking at him and saw that his complexion had changed. But they did not understand what he was saying,
because he was speaking in Hebrew, which they did not know. But the female musician understood everything, because she was a Hebrew woman,
and she kept looking at him. Even when she moved away from him and played music for the others, she still kept looking at him. She had grown fond of him as a man
from her own country. He was also more handsome in appearance than anyone else there. When the musician had finished, she sat down opposite him
and did not take her eyes off him. But he did not raise his eyes or look at anyone.
Instead, he kept looking at the ground until he should rise and leave the banquet hall. Meanwhile, that cupbearer had gone down to the spring to draw water.
A lion sprang upon him there, crushed him, and tore him apart limb by limb. Then dogs carried off his limbs, one by one.
One black dog carried his right hand—the one he had raised against Judas—and brought it into the middle of the banquet hall. When everyone saw it, they were astonished.
As they all asked who was missing from among them, it was discovered that the hand belonged to the cupbearer who had struck Judas.
Then the musician broke her pipes, came to the apostle’s feet, sat down, and said,
“This man is either God or an apostle of God. For I heard what he said in Hebrew to that cupbearer,
and it happened to him that very hour. For he said to him, ‘May I see the hand that struck me being dragged along by a dog.’
And now you have seen how a dog dragged it along.” Some of them believed the musician, and some did not.
When the king heard this news, he came and said to Judas, “Come with me and pray over my daughter,
because she is my only child, and today I am celebrating her wedding.” But he did not want to go with him, because our Lord had not yet appeared to him in that place.
But the king took him by force to the bridal chamber. He began to pray, saying, “Our Lord, companion of his servants,
guide and leader of those who believe in him, refuge and rest for the afflicted, hope of the poor, and savior of the weak,
healer of sick souls, giver of life to the worlds, and savior of created beings: you are the one who knows what is to come,
and you bring it to completion through us. You are the one who reveals hidden mysteries and discloses secret things. You are the planter of the good tree,
and through your hands all the servants came into being. You are hidden in all your servants and are made known through their deeds.
Jesus, the Son who brings perfect mercies to fulfillment, you became the Messiah and clothed yourself in the first man.
You are the power and wisdom, the knowledge, will, and delight of his Father. You were hidden in him in glory and revealed in him through your works.
You are one under two names. You appeared as someone weak, and those who saw you thought that you were a human being in need of help.
You showed the glory of your divinity through your spirit’s patience with our humanity, when you overthrew the Evil One from
his stronghold. You called the dead with your voice, and they lived. And to those who live and put their hope in you,
you promised an inheritance in your kingdom. You are the one who became a messenger and was sent from the heights above,
because you are able to carry out the living and perfect will of the one who sent you. Glorious are you, my Lord, in your power.
Your governance brings renewal throughout your creation and in all the works your divinity has fashioned. No other can fulfill the will of your greatness
or comprehend your being as you are. You descended to Sheol and reached its farthest depths. You opened its gates and brought up its prisoners.
You opened a road for them to the heights through the very being of your divinity. Yes, my Lord, I ask you on behalf of these young people: do for them whatever you know will help them.
He laid his hand on them and said to them, “May our Lord be with you.” He left them and went out. The king urged the wedding attendants to leave the bridal chamber.
When everyone had gone out and the door of the bridal chamber had been shut, the bridegroom lifted the curtain of the bridal chamber to bring the bride to him.
He saw our Lord in the likeness of Judas, standing and speaking with the bride. The bridegroom said to him, “Look, you were the first to leave! How are you here
still?” Our Lord said to him, “I am not [?] Judas, but I am Judas’s brother.” Our Lord sat down on the bed.
He invited the young people to sit on chairs and began to say to them, “Remember, my children, what my brother told you, and know to whom he entrusted you [?].
Know that as soon as you are freed from this filthy intercourse, you become pure temples.
You are freed from hidden and visible sufferings and from excessive anxiety about children, whose end is bitter distress.
And if you have sufferings, because of them you become oppressors, plunderers, and abusers of orphans, and you mistreat widows.
For children have many ailments: either the king attacks them, or a roof-demon seizes them,
or paralysis strikes them. And if they are healthy, they fall into sexual immorality, or greed, or empty boasting,
and through them you are implicated in these offenses. But if you obey me and keep yourselves pure for God,
you will have living children whom no blemish or harm approaches. You will be without anxiety, distress, or sorrow,
and you will look forward to seeing the true wedding feast, praising there, and being counted among those who enter the bridal chamber.”
The young people were persuaded by our Lord and entrusted themselves to him. They were freed from lust,
and they kept vigil in their places until dawn. Our Lord departed from them and said to them, “May the grace of your Lord be with you.”
In the morning, when dawn broke, the king rose early, prepared a laden table, and brought it in before the bridegroom and bride. He found them sitting.
Facing one another. The bride was sitting with her face unveiled, and the bridegroom too was very happy. The bride’s mother said to her:
“Why are you sitting like this, without any shame, as though you had already lived a long time and had many years of experience?”
Her father also said, “Because of your great love for your husband, you do not even veil yourself.” The bride answered and said to her mother:
“Truly, Mother, I am deeply in love, and I pray to my Lord that I may remain in this love that I experienced tonight.
And I will call upon the incorruptible bridegroom who appeared to me tonight. I am not veiled because the veil of corruption has been taken away from me. And I am not
ashamed because the act that brings shame has been removed from me. And I have no regret because the repentance that leads to life has remained within me.
And I am happy and rejoice because, on the day of this passing joy, I was not caught up in it.
For this act of corruption and the plunder of this fleeting wedding feast have become contemptible to me, because I have been invited to the true wedding feast.
And I have not been joined to a man in a union whose outcome is bitter remorse.” For she was saying things like these.
Then the bridegroom also answered and said, “I thank you, new God, who came here through the stranger.
I praise you, God, who are proclaimed through a Hebrew man, who kept me away from corruption and sowed life within me;
who delivered me from the sickness that would have remained in me forever; who showed himself to us, and I became aware of what I am;
who rescued me from ruin and brought me forward into virtue; who delivered me from the things that pass away and made me worthy of the things that do not pass away;
who reached down to my lowliness so that it might attain greatness; who did not withhold his mercy from me when I was lost,
but taught me to seek my own soul and removed from me what was not mine; who, when I did not know him, himself
sought me; who, when I was unaware of him, himself reached out to me; whom I have now come to perceive,
though I cannot say anything that I do not know. If I speak boldly about him, I will never finish, for it is because of his love that I am bold.”
When the king heard these things from the bridegroom and the bride, he tore his clothes and said to his attendants, “Go out quickly throughout the whole city.
Go around and bring me that man, that sorcerer whom I brought into my house with my own hands and told to pray for my ill-fated daughter [?]. Whoever finds him and brings him to me,
I will give him whatever he asks.” They went around looking for him, but they did not find him because he had departed. They went to the inn where he had been staying
and found the woman singer sitting and weeping because he had not taken her with him. When they told her what had happened, she rejoiced and said,
“I have found rest for myself here.” She got up and went to those young people, and she lived with them for a long time.
They also made the king [?] a disciple and gathered many brothers together, until news was heard of the apostle in the city of India. They went to him and joined him.
The first act is finished.
Second Act. The second act: When Thomas the apostle entered India and built a palace in heaven for the king.
When Judas entered the city of India with Habban the merchant, Habban went to greet Gondophares, the king of India, and told him about the skilled craftsman he had brought him.
The king was very pleased and ordered Judas to be brought before him. The king said to him, “What craft do you know how to practice?”
Judas said to him, “I am a carpenter, the servant of a carpenter, and a builder.” He said to him, “What do you know how to make?” Judas said to him:
“In wood I have learned to make yokes, ploughs, goads, oars for ferryboats and barges, and masts for ships.
And in cut stone, tombstones, monuments, and palaces for kings.” The king said to Judas, “That is just the kind of craftsman I am looking for.”
The king said to him, “Will you build me a palace?” Judas said to him, “I will build it and finish it. Indeed, I came to build and do carpentry.”
He took him along and went outside the city gate, talking with him about the work on the building
and about its foundations, how they should be laid. When he reached the place where the king wanted a palace built for him, he said to
Judas, “Here is where I want you to build me a palace.” Judas said to him, “Indeed, this is a suitable place for it.”
The place was like this: it was a meadow, with abundant water nearby. The king said to him, “Begin building here.”
Judas said to him, “I cannot build now, at this time of year.” The king said to him, “At what time of year can you build?”
Judas said, “I will begin in Tishri and finish in Nisan.” The king said to him, “All buildings are built in summer,
but you are going to build in winter?” Judas said to him, “That is how the palace can be built.” The king said to him,
“Then draw its plan for me so that I can see it, for it will be a long time before I come here again.” Judas came and took a measuring reed
and began to measure. He left room for doors on the east, for light, and windows on the west, for the breeze, and a bakery on the south,
and a water conduit on the north, for use in the building. The king said to him, “You truly are a good craftsman and worthy to serve a king.”
He left a large amount of silver with him and departed. He also sent him silver and gold from time to time. But Judas went around
the villages and cities, providing for the poor and bringing relief to those in distress.
He would say, “Let what belongs to the king be given to the king, and let there be relief for many.” After a long time,
the king sent messengers to Judas with this message: “Send me word of what you have accomplished and what I should send you.” Judas sent him word
that the palace was built and needed only a roof. Then the king sent silver and gold to Judas and sent him instructions
to put a roof on the palace. But Judas praised our Lord and said, “I thank you, my Lord, because you died to give me life,
and you sold me so that I might set many people free.” He did not stop teaching and bringing relief to those in distress,
saying, “Your Lord gives you rest. To him alone belongs glory, for he is the sustainer of orphans
and the provider for widows, and he provides for all who are in distress.” When the king came to the city,
He was asking each of his friends about the palace Judas had built for him. But they told him, “He has built no palace.
Nor has he done anything else. Instead, he has been going around the cities and villages, giving to the poor and teaching
them about a new God. He has also been healing the sick and driving out demons.
He has been doing many things, and we think he is a sorcerer. But his compassion, his healing—which was free of charge—
his ascetic life, and his piety suggest that he is either a magus or an apostle of a new God. For he fasts a great deal and prays a great deal.
He eats bread and salt and drinks water. He wears a single tunic and takes nothing from anyone.
Whatever he has, he gives to others.” When the king heard these things, he struck his face with his hands and shook his head.
He sent for Judas and the merchant who had brought him, and said to him, “Have you built me a palace?” Judas said to him, “I have built you a palace.”
The king said to him, “When shall we go and see it?” Judas said to him, “You cannot see it now, but only when you leave this world.”
Then the king became furious and ordered that Judas be bound, together with the merchant who had brought him,
and that they go to prison until they questioned him about what he had done—to whom he had given it—and then put him to death. But Judas went along rejoicing,
and said to the merchant, “Do not be afraid. Only believe firmly, and you will be freed from this world, and in the world to come you will receive eternal life.” But the king
was considering what kind of death he should inflict on Judas and the merchant. He was forming a plan
to strip him naked and burn him in the fire together with his companion, the merchant. That very night, the king’s brother, whose name was Gad,
became gravely ill from distress over the deception that had been inflicted on the king. He sent for the king and said to him, “My brother,
I entrust my household and my children to you. For I have become distressed over the deception inflicted on you, and I am dying. Unless you bring this down on that sorcerer’s head,
you will give my bones no rest in Sheol.” The king said to him, “All night I have been thinking about how to put him to death.
I have decided to strip him naked and burn him in the fire.” Then the king’s brother said to him, “If there is anything beyond that, do it to him. And I entrust my household and my children to you.”
When he had said these things, his soul left him. The king mourned his brother because he loved him very much, and he wanted to bury him in a fine tomb.
When the soul of Gad, the king’s brother, left him, angels took it and brought it up to heaven. They showed it the places one by one,
asking in which of them it wished to stay. Then, when they reached the palace Judas had built for the king, his brother saw it and said to those angels, “I beg
you, my lords, let me live in one of the lower rooms of this palace.” Those angels said to him,
“You cannot live in this palace.” He said to them, “Why?” They said to him, “This palace
is the one that Christian built for your brother.” Then he said to them, “I beg you, my lords, let me go to my brother
and buy this palace from him. For my brother knows nothing about it, and he will sell it to me.” Then the angels released Gad’s soul.
While they were dressing him, his soul returned to him, and he said to those standing before him,
“Call my brother for me, so that I may ask him one favor.” Then they brought the king the good news: “Your brother is alive!” The king sprang up from his place.
He went into his brother’s house with a large crowd. When he came before his bed, he was overwhelmed and could not speak to him.
His brother said to him, “I know, my brother, that if anyone had asked you for half your kingdom, you would have given it for my sake.
But now I ask you to sell me something you have worked for.” The king said to him,
“Tell me what I should sell you.” He said to him, “Swear to me.” And he swore that he would give him anything he asked for from all that he possessed. He said to him, “Sell me that palace
you have in heaven.” The king said to him, “A palace for me in heaven? Who gave it to me?” His brother said to him, “The one that Christian built for you.”
The king said to him, “I cannot sell you that one. But I pray and ask God
that I may enter it and receive it, and be worthy to become one of its inhabitants. But if you truly wish to buy yourself a palace,
this architect will build you one better than mine.” He sent and had Judas and the merchant who had been imprisoned with him brought out. He said to him, “I ask you,
as a man asks a servant of God, to pray for me and plead for me with the God whom you serve,
that he may forgive me for what I did to you and make me worthy to enter that palace you built for me. And I will become a servant of this God whom you proclaim.”
His brother also came and fell at the apostle’s feet. He said to him, “I ask you that I too may find mercy before your God
and be worthy to become his servant, and also receive what he showed me through the angels.” Judas said,
“I give thanks to you, our Lord Jesus Christ, because you alone are the true God, and there is no other. You know what no human being
knows. You have shown mercy to human beings, whom you willed into being and made, though they forgot you.
Yet you did not abandon them to the wolves. Shepherd them in your pastures, and give them water from your spring, which is never muddied and whose flow never ceases.
For look, they ask you and plead with you, and wish to become your servants, to be persecuted by your enemy, and to be hated for your sake.
So let them have confidence in you, be strengthened in your glorious mysteries, and receive from your generous gifts.”
They rejoiced in holy songs of praise and stayed close to the apostle, never leaving his side. Everyone who was in need received what they needed and found relief.
They asked him to let them receive the seal, saying to him, “While our souls are turned toward God, let us receive the seal.
For we have heard that all the sheep of the God whom you proclaim are known to him by the seal.” Judas said to them,
“I too rejoice, and I ask you to share in the Eucharist and also in the blessing of this Christ whom I proclaim.”
The king ordered that the bathhouse be closed for seven days and that no one bathe in it. When
the seven days were over, on the eighth day, all three of them entered the bathhouse at night so that Judas could baptize them.
Many lamps were shining in the building. And when they [?] to the bathhouse, Judas went in ahead of them.
Our Lord appeared to them and said to them, “Peace be with you, my brothers.” But they heard only a voice.
They did not see his appearance or who he was, for they had not yet been baptized. Judas went up and stood at the edge of the bathing pool.
He poured oil on their heads and said, “Come, holy name of Christ. Come, power of grace from on high. Come, mercies that bring perfection.
Come, exalted gift. Come, fellowship in blessing. Come, revealer of hidden mysteries. Come, mother of the seven houses,
whose rest is in the eighth house. Come, messenger of reconciliation [?], and share in the thoughts of these young men. Come, Holy Spirit,
and cleanse their kidneys and their hearts.” He baptized them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. And when they came up out of the water,
a young man appeared to them, holding a shining candle. Its light made the light of those lamps grow dim.
When they went outside, he disappeared from their sight. And the apostle said, “We could not even bear your light,
because it is beyond what our eyes can bear.” When day broke and morning came, he broke the Eucharistic bread and gave them a share in Christ’s table.
They were enjoying themselves and rejoicing. And many more were joining them and coming to Christ’s house of refuge.
Judas did not stop preaching and saying to them, “Men, women, and children, young men and virgins,
keep away from sexual immorality, greed, and the worship of demons. For all wickedness arises from these three main things.
Sexual immorality blinds the mind and darkens the eye of the soul. It disrupts the body’s movements and changes its complexion,
and makes it sick. Greed keeps the soul in turmoil within the body, as it takes what does not belong to it,
and fears that, when it returns what it has taken to its owners, it will be put to shame. But service of the belly [?] makes it dwell in worry and distress [?]. And it changes its complexion,
and makes it sick. Greed keeps the soul in turmoil within the body, as it takes what does not belong to it,
and fears that, when it returns what it has taken to its owners, it will be put to shame. But service of the belly makes the soul dwell in worry and distress,
as it fears that it may lack something and reaches out for things far from it. For when you have been freed from these things,
you will be without worry and without distress. And this saying will remain with you: ‘Do not worry about tomorrow, because tomorrow will worry about itself.’
And remember that other saying written for you: ‘Look at the ravens and consider the birds of the sky: they neither sow nor reap, yet God feeds them.’
How much more, then, will he care for you, you who have little faith! But wait for the coming of Jesus, place your hope in him, and believe
in his name. For he is the judge of the dead and the living, and he will repay everyone according to their deeds at his final coming.
For there is no excuse for anyone to say, ‘We did not know.’ His heralds proclaim in the four corners of the world: ‘Repent and believe in the new good news.
Accept the gentle yoke and the light burden. Live, and do not die. Gain, and do not lose. Come out of darkness, and the light will welcome you.’
Come to the Good One and receive grace for yourselves, and fix his sign in your souls. While the apostle was saying these things,
some of them said to him, “It is time for the debtor, too, to settle his debt.” He said to them, “The creditor always asks for more.
But let us give him what is due.” He blessed the bread and olives and gave them to them, and he himself ate, for Sunday was dawning.
While the apostle was sleeping at night, our Lord came and stood over him and said to him, “Thomas, get up and go out at dawn, after the service,
and go about two miles along the eastern road. I will reveal my glory through you, for this is why you are setting out.
Many will come to a place of refuge and live, and you will rebuke the power and nature of the Enemy.” When he awoke from his sleep, he said to the brothers who were with him,
“My children, our Lord will do what he wishes today. But let us pray and ask him that nothing may hinder us in our relationship with him. Rather,
just as he wishes at all times to reveal his glory through us, so now too may his will be fulfilled.” When he had said this,
he laid his hand on them, broke the Eucharistic bread, and gave it to them all, saying to them,
“May this Eucharist bring you grace and mercy, and not judgment and punishment.” And they said, “Amen.”
The second act is ended.
Third Act. Again, the third act of Judas, concerning the black snake.
The apostle went out to go where our Lord had told him. When he had traveled two miles, he turned a little aside from the road
and saw the body of a handsome young man lying there. He said, “Our Lord, was it for this trial that you brought me out here?
Let it be as you wish.” He began to pray, saying, “Our Lord, master of the dead and the living,
the living who stand here and the dead who lie here; Lord, master of the souls that dwell in bodies, and Father of all the souls
that have departed from the body: come, my Lord, at this hour, for the sake of the dust that your holy hands formed. Look down from heaven, for I am calling
to you, and reveal your glory in this man who lies here.” He also said, “This deed did not happen without the interference of the Enemy who does these things.
Yet the Enemy who does these things would not dare attack someone who was a stranger to him, unless that person had surrendered to his will.”
While he was saying these things, a black snake came out of a hole, holding its head up
and beating its tail against the ground. In a loud voice it said to the apostle, “I will tell you why I killed this young man.
There is a beautiful woman in this village opposite you. As she passed by me, I saw her and fell in love with her.
I followed her and saw this young man kissing her. He even slept with her
and did other things with her that are not proper, though they are trivial to me. But I dare to tell you about them,
because I know that the [?] of Christ destroys our nature. So as not to disturb her, I did not kill him at that time.
But I waited for him, and in the evening, when he passed by me, I struck him and killed him, especially because he had dared to do this deed
on Sunday. Judas said to him, “What stock do you come from?” The serpent said to him, “I am a creeping creature, the son of a creeping creature,
and a harmful creature, the son of a harmful creature. I am the son of the one who was given authority over creation and threw it into turmoil.
I am the son of the one who appears like God to those who obey him and do his will.
I am the son of the one who rules over everything created beneath heaven. I am the son of the one who is beyond the ocean, whose mouth is sealed.
I am of the family of the one who spoke with Eve, and through her I caused Adam to transgress God’s commandment.
I am the one who incited Cain to kill his brother. Because of me—for this very purpose I was created—the earth was cursed, and thorns sprang up in it.
I am the one who acted boldly and cast the righteous down from their heights, and through desire for women I led them into sin.
I brought forth children with enormous bodies, and I carried out my will through them. I am the one who hardened Pharaoh’s heart so that he would kill the children of Israel
and subject them to harsh slavery. I am the one who incited Caiaphas and [?] to slander the righteous judge. I am the one
who made Judas accept a bribe, when he became subject to me, to hand Christ over to death.
I am the one who was given authority over this world, and the Son of Mary led me away by force and took what belonged to him away from me.
I am of the family of the one who comes from the east, to whom authority has been given.” The serpent said these things
because Judas had asked our Lord that it be given speech, so that it would be compelled to speak about its nature. When it finished, the crowd had heard everything.
Fear, together with faith, settled upon everyone there when they saw and heard these wonders. They cried out together with one voice,
“The God of this man is one! He has shown us about his God, and by his word he commanded this frightening beast, and it revealed its nature.”
They asked him that, just as he had commanded it by his word to speak like a human being, he should also kill it by his word.
Then Judas motioned to them with his hand, raised his voice, and said, “You act boldly, though your nature is exposed and you are condemned to death. Your appointed limit has arrived,
not so that you may tell what you have done through those who obeyed you. You were not afraid that your end had arrived. But I tell you,
in the name of our Lord Jesus, who struggled to the end against your nature on behalf of his own people: draw out the venom that you poured into this young man.
For he [?] sent me to kill you and raise him alive before this crowd, so that they may believe in him, that he is the true God and there is no other.”
The serpent said to him, “Our end has not yet arrived, as you said. Why are you forcing me to take back what I put into this young man?
For even my father, when he draws out and takes back what he has poured into creation, will meet his end.” The apostle said to it,
“Then reveal your father’s nature.” The serpent came and placed its mouth over the young man’s wound and began drawing the venom out of him.
Little by little, as the venom was drawn out, the young man’s complexion, which had become purple, grew pale, while the serpent swelled up.
And when he had drawn all his venom out of that young man, the young man sprang up, stood, and ran to the apostle’s feet. He fell down and bowed before him.
Then that serpent burst at Judas’s word. And in the place where the serpent’s venom had fallen, a great pit appeared.
Judas instructed the king and his brother to fill that place, lay foundations, and build houses there as lodgings
for strangers. Meanwhile, the young man was praising God, by whose mercy he had been restored to life through Judas the apostle.
He was freed from all his former deeds, and he asked the apostle to help him by praying to our Lord.
He collected himself and said, “Glory to you, merciful, great, and glorious God, maker and fashioner of all creatures.
You established a boundary and a measure for all your creatures that you created. You established a boundary and a measure for all your creatures that you created.
You established a boundary and a measure for all your creatures that you created, and you gave them differences that support their natures.
You are the one who made the human being as your divinity wished, fashioning him with your hands, so that he might rule above. And you created another creature for him,
so that he might struggle against it with the freedom you gave him. But the human being forgot his free nature and became enslaved to his fellow servant, who became his enemy,

because he found that the human being had forgotten his freedom. The enemy rejoiced that he had found a way to gain access to his fellow servant, and he expected to become master over all the servants.
But you, merciful one, in your great compassion spread your grace over us, and you sent to our human race
your word, which orders all creatures, through your glorious Son. And he, with the freedom you gave him and with your grace helping him,
came and found us engaged in those deeds that our humanity had practiced from the first day. You did not punish us for our sins, but brought us to life
by your grace. You showed us my weakness and planted your heavenly love in me. You opened my mouth, which had been shut, so that I could speak about the one who enslaved me
and about your abundant mercy. He does not silence me for what I say about him, for I speak because of his great love.”
Judas stretched out his hand to him and raised him up. He embraced him and said to him, “May our Lord’s mercy be with you
and with all who believe in him.” And the young man said, “Glory to you, God, who did not withhold his compassion from me when I was lost,
but showed me that I should seek my soul’s salvation. He made known to me that you are his apostle, and he said to you, ‘I have many things to reveal through your hands,
and you have many deeds to accomplish through me, for which you will receive a reward. You will bring many to life,
and they will be children of God in the light on high.’ Therefore, restore this young man to life, who was struck by his enemy, because you always see your Lord.
Yes, my lord, apostle of God, you did well to come here and draw many to him. Nor does he withdraw from you.
I have become free of worry and suffering because of his grace, which came upon me through your hand, and his gift has been poured out upon my weakness.
I have come to my senses, away from evil thoughts and destructive deeds. I have come to my senses, away from the one who was enticing me and urging me to do those things in which you found me.
I have understood the one who was telling me to do the opposite, and I have got rid of the one who was bewildering me with his deeds in the darkness, his own kin [?].”
And I found that light, the lord of the day, who had not been visible to me, and I saw him.
And I destroyed the one who darkened and blinded all those who followed him and obeyed him,
so that they would not see what they were doing, become ashamed of their deeds, and turn away from them, bringing his work to an end.
But I found the one who acts in such a way that those who do his will never regret it.
I escaped from the one supported by falsehood, with concealment going before him and shame following behind him,
while it acts brazenly and shamelessly. But I found the one who exposes evil deeds, the lord of peace and the one who establishes truth.
He drives the enemy away from those who turn to him, heals their sufferings, and overthrows the one who troubles them. But I ask you, apostle of God:
Sow your word of life in me, so that I may once again hear fully the voice of the one who entrusted me to you and said to you,
“This man is one of those who receive life through your hands. From now on, let him be with you.” Judas said to him:
“If you free yourself from these things you learned, as you said, from that doer of evil,
and obey the one whom you have now sought in the fervor of your love, you will see him and be with him forever.
You will find rest with him in his mercy and share in his joy. But if you neglect him
and return to those former deeds of yours and to the one whom you now insult because of the beauty and the appearance of the light
of this one whom you long for, you will not only be deprived of that life you have seen,
but you will also lose what you now have.” Judas was coming into the city, and he took that young man by the hand
and said to him, “My son, these things you have seen are small compared with the many things our God has.
For he does not give us hope in these visible things, but promises better things. For as long as we are in the world, we cannot
speak of what all God's faithful people are to receive. For if we say that he gives us wealth,
we are speaking of something that exists in the world. And if we speak of clothing, we are speaking of what great men wear.
And if we speak of exquisite foods, we are speaking of things from which we have abstained. And if we speak of temporary comfort,
punishment hangs over it. Instead, we speak of God and our Lord Jesus, of angels, watchers, and holy ones,
of the new world, of the [?] of the tree of life, and of the drink of life—of what no eye has seen and no ear has heard,
and what has not entered the human heart, what God prepared long ago for those who love him. This is what we speak about,
and this is what we proclaim. So believe in him, my son, so that you may live, and put your hope in him so that you may not die.
For he accepts no bribe that you might offer him, nor does he desire sacrifices that you might sacrifice to him. Look to him, and he will not neglect you.”
Turn toward him, and he will not let you go. For his beauty draws you to love him, and he will not let you turn away from him.
While Judas was saying these things to that young man, large crowds kept gathering. The apostle raised his eyes and saw the people
climbing above one another to see him. They were going up to high places to see him. The apostle said to them:
“Men who have come to the meeting place of Christ, people who wish to believe in Jesus, learn a lesson from this:
unless you raise yourselves up, you cannot see even me, insignificant as I am. You cannot see me, although I am just like you.
How can you see the one who is on high and is found in the depths, unless you rise above your former deeds,
and above actions that bring no benefit, desires that do not last, and wealth [?] that perishes and is left here,
and above property and possessions that come to an end on earth, clothes that wear out, and beauty that grows old and becomes ugly,
and above the body in which all these things are contained, which becomes dust? All these things depend on it. But believe and put your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ,
whom we proclaim, so that your hope may be directed toward him and you may live in him forever and ever. He will be your guide in a place of error.
He will be your harbor on a troubled sea. He will be your spring of living water in a place of thirst.
He will be your full basket in a place of hunger. He will be rest for your souls, and a healer and giver of life
to your bodies.” Then the crowds cried out, “Apostle of the living God, guide to the way of life, and revealer of the mysteries of truth!
We have done many things that are foreign to the glorious God whom you proclaim.
Even now we do not dare to say that we belong to him, because our deeds are foreign to him and hateful in his sight.
But if he has mercy on us and delivers us from our former actions and from the evil things we did in error, and does not reject us or hold our former sins against us,
we will become his servants and carry out his will.” Judas said to them, “He does not hold against you the sins you committed in error.
Instead, he forgives your former offenses, which you committed unknowingly.”
[The Third Act is finished.]
Fourth Act. [Again, the Fourth Act.] While the apostle stood in his place on the road, speaking with those crowds about the kingdom of God,
and about their turning and repentance toward our Lord—while the apostle stood on the road and was speaking with those crowds,
a colt, the young of a donkey, came and stood before him. Judas said, “It is not without God's providence that this colt has come here.
But I say to you, colt: may you be given speech by the grace of our Lord before these crowds standing here.
Say whatever you wish, so that they may believe in the God of truth whom we proclaim.” Then that colt's mouth was opened,
and it spoke like a human being by the power of our Lord. It said to him, “Twin of Christ and apostle of the Most High, and sharer in the secret word of the Giver of Life!”
And you who receive the hidden mysteries of the Son of God, a freeborn man who became a slave so that through his obedience he might bring many to freedom.
Son of a numerous family who became deprived, so that by the power of your Lord you might deprive the enemy of many.
So that you might become a source of life for the land of the Indians—you who came against your will to people who had wandered away from God.
And now, through the sight of you and your divine words, they are turning toward life. Climb up, ride on me, and rest until you enter the city.” Judas raised his voice and said:
“O Jesus, Son of perfect mercy! O quiet and silent one, you speak through animals that have no speech! O
hidden one who is seen through his works! We are nourished and protected. Giver of life to our bodies and giver of life to our souls,
sweet spring that never runs dry, and clear fountain that is never muddied! He becomes a helper to his servants in the contest,
and tears the enemy apart before them. He stands in the contests on our behalf and gives us victory in them all. Our champion of truth, who cannot be harmed,
and our holy commander, who cannot be defeated! He gives his own people joy that does not pass away, and rest in which there is no further distress.
The good shepherd who gave his life for his flock, who defeated the wolf and rescued his lambs!
We praise you, and through you we exalt your Father on high, who cannot be seen, and the Spirit of holiness, who hovers over all created things.”
When the apostle said these things, all the crowds gathered there were watching to see what answer he would give that colt.
After the apostle had stood for a long time in wonder, looking toward heaven, he said to that colt:
“Who are you, and what is your story, that wonders have been spoken through your mouth, and great things surpassing many others?”
That colt said to him, “I belong to the family that served Balaam the prophet, and your Lord God rode on one of my stock.
I was sent to you to give you rest, and so that through this the faith of these people might be turned back to God.
And may that other portion be added to me, which I acquired today because I was to serve you. Why should it be taken away from me because I have served you?”
Thomas said to him, “God, who has now given you this gift, is faithful, so that in the life to come it will also be fulfilled for you and the members of your family.
For I am too small and weak for this mystery.” And he did not want to ride on him. But that colt kept asking him and pleading with him
to be blessed by his riding on him. So he climbed up and rode him. People were coming behind the apostle and ahead of him,
and were running to see what would happen to him and how he would dismiss that colt. When he reached the city gate, he got down from him
and said to him, “Go, and remain as you were.” At that very moment the colt fell down and died.
Everyone who was there grieved over him, and they said to the apostle, “Bring him back to life.” The apostle said to them:
“It is not because I cannot bring this colt back to life that I do not revive him. Rather, this is what benefits him. For the one who gave him speech
could have kept him from dying. But this is what benefits him.” And the apostle ordered those who were with him to dig.
a place, and bury his body. And they did as he had commanded them.
[The fourth act is finished.]

Fifth Act [Again, the fifth act.] The apostle entered the city with those crowds accompanying him. He was thinking of going to the home of the family of the young man whom he had brought back to life.
For he had begged him earnestly. A beautiful woman cried out in a loud voice and said to him, “Apostle of the new God who has come to India,

servant of the holy God who is proclaimed through you, the giver of life, the giver of life to the souls of those who come to him, and the healer of the bodies of those who are tormented by the enemy,
who has become the source of life for all the people of India, allow them to bring me before you, so that I may tell you what has happened to me.
Perhaps through you I may have hope, and those standing here may be strengthened still more in the God whom you proclaim.
I tell you that I have been severely tormented by the enemy for five years now. I had been living quietly, and peace surrounded
me on every side. I was not worried about anything, for I did not even know what worry was. But one day, as I was coming out of the bathhouse,
a man met me whose appearance seemed disturbed. His tone and the sound of his voice were very gentle.
He said to me, ‘Let you and me be united in one love. Join with me in the union of a man and a woman.’
I said to him, ‘I did not give myself to my betrothed, because I cannot bear a man. As for you, who want to join with me in adultery,
how could I give myself to you?’ And I said to the girl who was with me, ‘Look at that young man’s shamelessness,
that he should speak to me so openly!’ But she said to me, ‘I saw an old man speaking with you.’ When I went home and had supper,
my heart was troubled because of him, since he had appeared to me in two forms. I went to sleep thinking about him. During the night he came and joined with me in a filthy union.
I would also see him during the day and flee from him.
But at night he would come upon me terrifyingly and torment me. And even now, as you see me, it has been five years, and he has not left me alone. But because I know
and believe that demons, spirits, and devils are all subject to you and fear your prayer,
I ask you, my lord, to pray for me and petition God, and to drive this affliction away from me, so that for the time remaining to me I may be free,
return to my original nature, and receive the gift that is given to those who repent.” Then, when the apostle saw the enemy’s relentless activity,
he raised his voice and said, “O evil that never tires! O enemy that never stops! O envy that has no rest!
O ugly one, you who fight against the beautiful to subdue them beneath you! O you who have many ugly forms
and appear however you wish! Yet your black color does not change, because it is your nature. O crafty one, who confounds good deeds!
O you who have many ugly forms and appear however you wish! Yet your black color does not change,
because it is your nature. O crafty one, who confounds good deeds! O bitter tree whose fruits resemble it!
O lying devil, who fights over what is not his! O delusion, which, even when thrown down on its head, stands defiantly!
And it acts insolently toward those better than itself. O wickedness, slippery as a snake, which crawls and enters and reaches out toward virtue!
How long shall I say these things? Instead, show yourself quickly, enemy of Christ’s servants,
so that these crowds whom we are calling to the God of truth may see.” While the apostle was saying these things, that enemy came
and stood before him. No one could see him except the apostle himself and that woman. He cried out in a loud voice,
while everyone who was there could hear him: “What have we to do with you, apostle of the Most High? What have we to do with you, servant of Jesus Christ?
What have we to do with you, confidant in God’s holy mysteries? Why do you want to destroy us when our time has not yet come?
Why do you seek to take away the authority given to us, while we still have hope in it? What have we to do with you, that you have come to drive us out?
You have authority over those who obey you, and we have authority over those who fall to our lot.
Why have you chosen to drive us away by force before our time, when you command others, ‘Do not force anyone’?
Why do you covet what is not yours? Are your own not enough for you? Why do you imitate your Lord God,
who concealed his greatness and appeared in a body? We thought he was mortal, but he turned around and drove us away by force.
Indeed, it is as though you were born of him. For when we thought we would bring him under our authority, he turned around and hurled us into the depths.
For we did not know him. He deceived us with his humble appearance, his neediness, and his poverty. When we saw him, we thought he was one of
humankind, and we did not know that he was the giver of life to all humanity. Yet he gave us authority not to relinquish what is ours for as long as our time lasts.
And we were making use of what was ours. But now you have chosen to acquire more than what he gave you, and to cause us suffering.”
While that demon was saying these things, he also wept and said, “I am leaving you, my beautiful companion,
whom I found long ago and upon whom I rested. I am leaving you, my sister and my beloved, with whom I hoped to remain.
I do not know what to do. Whom, indeed, shall I call to help me? I know what I will do: I will go away to another place,
where news of this man has not been heard. I will seek you out, my beloved.” Then he raised his voice and said,
“Remain without peace, you who have taken refuge in someone greater than I! I am going away to wander and seek someone like myself.
And if I find no one, I will return to you again. For I know that now, because this man is near you,
you have taken refuge in him. But I am leaving here, and you will remain as you are, so that when night comes, you will forget him,
and I, for my part, will take revenge on you. For now it is the name of the one whom I proclaim that has frightened me.” And while
that demon was saying these things, he was immediately sought but could not be found. Only smoke and fire were seen behind him.
All those standing there were amazed. When the apostle saw this, he said to them, “That accursed one has shown nothing unusual.
Rather, it is the nature in which he was destroyed, for fire destroys him, and smoke rises from him.” Then the apostle began to say:
“Jesus, hidden mystery revealed to me, you are the one who disclosed your mysteries to me more than to all my companions.
You spoke words to me with which I am now burning, yet I cannot utter them. Jesus, a human being, born,
killed, dead. Jesus, God, Son of God, giver of life, who raises the dead. Jesus, needy, catching fish for breakfast and supper.
Jesus, who feeds many thousands with a little bread. Jesus, who rests from the [?] of the journey like a human being,
and walks on the waves of the sea like God. Jesus, exalted voice that dawned from perfect compassion,
Savior of all, liberator, provider for the world, and strengthener of the dead. Jesus, right hand of the Father, you who cast the evil one down to the lowest region,
and gathered his possessions into one blessed [?]. Jesus, King over all, to whom everything is subject. Jesus, you are in the Father and the Father is in you, and
you are one in power, will, glory, and being. For our sake you were called by various names, though you are the Son, and you clothed yourself in a body.
Jesus, you became an ascetic, and your grace provides for everyone, as God. Son of the Most High God, you became a despised and humble human being.
Jesus, who does not neglect us in what we ask of him, you became the source of life for all humanity. Jesus, you were called a deceiver for our sake.
You are the one who removes your people from error. I ask you on behalf of these who stand here and believe in you,
who need your help, await your gift, take refuge in your greatness, and open their ears to hear your words spoken through us.
May your grace come, and may your faithfulness rest upon them and renew them from their former deeds.
May they put off their old self with its deeds and put on the new self, who is now being proclaimed to them through me.”
He laid his hand on them, blessed them, and said to them, “May the grace of our Lord be upon you forever and ever. Amen.”
The woman pleaded with him, saying, “Apostle of the Most High, give me the seal of my Lord,
so that the enemy will not return against me again.” He went to a river nearby and baptized her in the name of the Father and the Son and the Spirit
of Holiness. Many others were also baptized with her. The apostle instructed his attendant to prepare the portions. He brought a bench there and spread a linen cloth over it.
He brought the bread of blessing and placed it on it. The apostle came, stood over it, and said:
“Jesus, you have made us worthy to approach your holy body and to share in your life-giving blood. Because of our trust in you, we boldly draw near
and invoke your holy name, which was proclaimed through the prophets as your divinity willed. You are proclaimed through your apostles throughout the world according to your grace,
and in your compassion you revealed yourself to the righteous. We ask you to come and share with us, for help and life, and so that your servants may turn to you,
so that they may come under your gentle yoke and your victorious power, and that this may bring healing to their souls and life to their bodies in your living world.”
And he began to say: “Come, gift of the Most High. Come, perfect mercies. Come, Holy Spirit.
Come, revealer of the mysteries [?] of the chosen one among the prophets. Come, proclaimer through his apostles of the contests of the victorious athlete. Come, treasure of greatness.
Come, beloved of the mercies of the Most High. Come, silent one who reveals the mysteries of the Most High. Come, speaker of hidden things,
and revealer of the works of our God. Come, giver of joy and rest to all who follow her.
Come, power of the Father and wisdom of the Son, for you are one in everything. Come and share with us in this Eucharist that we celebrate,
and in this offering that we present, and in this remembrance that we perform.” And he traced a cross over the bread and began to distribute it.
He gave it first to that woman and said to her, “May it be for you for the forgiveness of debts and sins, and for resurrection to eternal life.”
After her, he gave it to those people who had been baptized with her. Then he gave it to everyone and said to them,
“May this Eucharist be for you for life and rest, and not for judgment and punishment.” And they said, “Amen.”
[The fifth act is finished.]
Sixth Act [Again, the sixth act.] Now there was a young man there who had committed
a very vile act [?]. He came and took the Eucharist, and went to put it into his mouth, but both his hands withered
and could not reach his mouth. When some of those who were with him saw him, they came and told the apostle what had happened to him.
The apostle called him and said to him, “Tell me, my son, and do not be ashamed before me. What have you done and brought here now? For look, the gift of our Lord has rebuked you.
This gift heals the many who receive it in love, truth, and faith, but in your case it has utterly withered you.
It was not without cause [?] that these things happened to you.” When that young man saw that he had been rebuked by the Eucharist of our Lord, he came and fell at the apostle’s feet.
He begged him and pleaded before him, saying to him, “I had done an evil deed.
I loved a woman at an inn outside the city, and she too loved me [?]. Because I had heard from you the truth that you speak
and the faith in God that you proclaim, and knew truly that you are God’s apostle, I too had received the seal
with those who received it. And I said this: ‘Whoever from now on engages in unclean intercourse,
especially adultery, has no life with this God whom you proclaim.’ And because I loved her,
I had begged her and urged her to live with me a pure, holy, peaceful, chaste, and humble life,
the life that you teach. But she was unwilling. When I saw that she would not be persuaded by me, I struck her down and killed her,
because I could not bear to see her having intercourse with other men.” When the apostle heard these things, he said,
“O unrestrained love of corruption! How you have stirred this man to do these things! O shameless intercourse!”
How it corrupts people's minds, turning them away from the holiness of Christ! Oh, the work of error! How greatly it exalts itself through its own doing!
The apostle ordered them to bring him water in a washing basin. They brought him water so that he could pray over it, and he gave praise and blessed it, saying:
“Water given to us from the living water; light [?] sent to us from the glorious Being; compassion sent to us from the Compassionate One: let your victorious power come.
Let your healing and your mercy rest and dwell upon this water, over which I have proclaimed your name, Jesus our Life-giver.”
And he said, “May the gift of the Holy Spirit be fulfilled in you.” Then he said to that
young man, “Go and wash your hands in that water.” He went and washed his hands, and they became as they had been before they withered.
The apostle said to him, “Do you believe, then, in our Lord, that everything is within his power to do?” The young man said to him:
“I was not lacking in faith. Indeed, it was because I believed in God that I committed this deed, thinking that I had done well.
For I was asking her, as I told you before, but she would not listen to me and keep herself in purity and chastity.
That is why I did this to her.” Judas said to him, “Come, let us go to the inn where you committed this deed.”
He walked ahead of the apostle, and a large crowd followed him. When they arrived
at the inn, they went inside and found the woman dead. When the apostle saw her, he grieved over her,
because she was young. He told them to lift her up and bring her out into the middle of the inn. When they had brought her and laid her on a bed,
Judas Thomas placed his hand on her and began to say, “Jesus our Life-giver, who never neglects us whenever we call upon him;
Jesus, who comes to us whenever we seek him: you are the one whose ear is inclined to this, that we should ask you, and you give
to us. Jesus, who not only permitted us to ask, but also taught us how to pray; who is not now visible to these bodily eyes of ours, yet is not absent from the eyes of our understanding;
who is hidden from our sight, yet whose grace is revealed to us, along with his care for his servants and his many deeds;
whom we have known as far as we are able, according to our capacity, yet who has given us his gift beyond our capacity; who said, ‘Ask, and it will be given to you.
Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you.’ We therefore ask you, our Lord, while we fear because of our offenses and our sins,
to spread your compassion over us in your mercy. We do not seek gold or silver or wealth or possessions,
or property or clothing, or anything at all among these earthly things that belong to time, come into being from it, and return to it.
Rather, we ask you and appeal to your kindness to raise up, in your holy name, this woman who lies before you, for your great praise and the acknowledgment of your divinity,
and to strengthen the faith in you of those standing here.” Then he said to the young man, “Direct your mind toward our Lord.”
He marked him with the sign of the cross and said to him, “Go, take her by the hand, and say to her, ‘I killed you with my own hands, with an iron weapon. But Jesus, in his compassion,
through my faith, raises you up.’” The young man went and stood over her, saying, “I have truly believed in you, my Lord Jesus Christ, the gift of his Father.”
For in you is every kind of help, in you every provision, in you every cure, and in you life for those who repent,
who truly turn to you with all their heart. Yes, my Lord, I ask your mercy: come to my aid and bring about my own restoration.
Give this woman life through my hands, as I dare to do this.” He looked at Judas Thomas and said to him, “Pray for me, apostle of God,
that my Lord may come to my aid, as I [?] him.” He placed his hand on hers and said, “Come, my Lord Jesus Christ, and give this woman life,
and give me a pledge of faith in you.” Immediately, when he took hold of her hand, she sprang up, stood, and looked at the great crowd standing there.
She saw the apostle of our Lord standing opposite her, and she ran and fell at his feet.
She held onto the hems of his clothing and said to him, “I beg you, my lord, where is that other man who was with you,
who would not let me remain in the place I saw, but handed me over to you and said to you, ‘Take this woman; let her go with you,
so that she may be perfected in her love through faith, and then she will be gathered into my place’?” Judas said to her,
“Tell me where you went and what you saw.” She said to him, “You were with me, and he handed me over to you! Do you want to hear it from me?”
She began to tell him, “A man took me away. He was ugly in appearance, his body was black, and his clothing was repulsive.
He brought me to a place full of pits, and a foul smell also filled it.
He made me look into each of the pits. I saw the first pit, with what looked like a blazing fire inside it, and wheels of fire revolving within it.
He told me that souls who transgress the law, changing the marriage partnership established by God, are destined to come to this torment.
Others too are destined to come to this torment: those who did not preserve their virginity but gave themselves over to shameful deeds. They come to this affliction
because they transgressed God's law. They are handed over to evil spirits and become objects of laughter and mockery, and punishment is exacted from them.
They go to another torment worse than this and are tormented there. Then he showed me another pit, and I looked into it
and saw terrible things, to which souls that do evil are destined to come.
There I saw many scourges prepared for men and women, young men and virgins:
those men who leave their wives and have intercourse with their companions' wives; women who violate their marriage partnership with their husbands;
and young men who did not observe their laws but indulged their lust with prostitutes. They were not satisfied with the lawlessness of the brothel,
but lay in wait for virgins and indulged in sin. Virgins who did not preserve their virgin state, but through their unrestrained lust brought shame on their fathers,
also come to this affliction. Everyone is repaid according to their deeds.
Again he led me on and showed me a dark cave, from which a foul smell was coming. He said to me, ‘Look inside and see,
for this is the prison of those souls I told you about. When the punishment of each one of them is finished, another takes its place.’
Some of them are completely consumed, while others are handed over to other torments. They say to the man who was leading me,
those guardians of the torments, “Give this woman to us so that we may confine her in her place, for she is going to her torment.” The man who was leading me says to them, “I will not
give her to you, because I fear the one who entrusted her to me. Nor was I instructed [?] to leave her here.
Instead, I am taking her up with me until I receive a command concerning her.” Then the one who resembled you led me away and handed me over to you. He said to you, “Take this woman,
because she is one of those sheep that have strayed.” You took me from him, and here I stand before you.
I ask you that I too may come to believe through you, and receive mercy because of your prayer, and that I too may not go to those torments that I saw.
Judas Thomas said to them, “My children, you have heard what this woman said. And these are not the only torments that exist,
but there are also others far worse than these. So you too, unless you turn to this truth that I proclaim,
and turn away from your evil deeds, from your actions that bring you no benefit, and from your ignorant thoughts,
your end will lead you to these very torments. But believe in Jesus Christ,
and he will wipe away your former deeds and cleanse you of all your earthly thoughts,
which remain on earth. He will forgive your sins, which, unless you turn from them to God,
will accompany you, go with you, and be found before you. So let each one of you strip off the old self
and put on the new self. As for those former ways of yours and your bodily deeds, let those who used to steal
steal no longer, but toil and work and live. And let those among you who used to commit adultery no longer commit adultery
or be deceived by a moment’s pleasure, so that they do not go to everlasting torment. For adultery is hateful before God,
more than all other evil practices. Put away from yourselves falsehood, oppression, drunkenness, and slander.
Do not inflict malicious harm on anyone. For all these things, to this God whom I proclaim,
are hateful and unclean. Instead, conduct yourselves with all humility, self-restraint, and holiness,
and with hope in God. You will become members of his household and receive gifts from him, which are given to each person.”
Those crowds had believed and entrusted themselves to the living God and to Jesus Christ. They delighted in the blessed works
of the Most High and in his holy service. Each of them brought a great deal of money for the relief of the widows
who had been gathered around the apostle in each city. Through his servants he sent all of them whatever they needed for food and clothing.
He never stopped preaching, speaking to them, and showing them that this is Jesus Christ,
of whom the Scriptures spoke, and whose foreshadowings, mysteries, and images the Law and the Prophets revealed, a covenant having been given to the people.
that, because of him, they might be prevented from having God's grace descend upon them. All who keep his commandments rest in his kingdom and are honored with glory.
He came, was crucified, and rose after three days. He recounted and explained these things to them, beginning with Moses and continuing to the last of the prophets.
For they had all proclaimed him, and he came and fulfilled it in deeds. His fame spread among people in cities and villages.
And everyone who had someone sick, or someone possessed by a spirit, or suffering from trembling, or whose limbs were withered—
some of them they would bring on beds and lay along the road wherever they learned he was going. He healed them all through the power of Jesus his Lord.
The sick who suffered from severe illnesses and terrible torments were healed, as were the paralyzed, who stood firmly on their feet.
They all praised with one voice, saying, “Glory to you, Jesus Christ, who have given us healing through your servant and apostle Judas.
For now that we are well and can see, we ask you that we too may belong to your fold and be counted among your [?].
Accept us, our Lord, and do not hold our former sins against us, for we committed them in ignorance.” Then, when Judas Thomas saw them,
he raised his voice and said, “Glory to you, the living one who comes from the living one. Glory to you, giver of life to many.
Glory to you, the strength and helper of those who come to your refuge. Glory to you, the eternally watchful one, who awakens human beings.
Living and life-giving one, you are God, the Son of God, the Savior and helper, the haven and rest of all who have grown weary in his service,
who gives rest to those who, for his name's sake, have borne the burden of the whole day in the midday heat. We thank you for your gift toward [?],
and for your help in our weakness, and for your provision for our poverty. Continue your grace and mercy toward us until
the end, and give us confidence in you. See, my Lord, that we have loved you alone.
See, my Lord, that we have left our homes and these households of ours, and for your sake have become strangers without compulsion. See, my Lord, that we have left our possessions for your sake,
so that we may gain you as a possession of life that cannot be taken away. See, our Lord, that we have left all our humanity for your sake, so that we may be united with your own humanity.
See, our Lord, that we have left our fathers, our mothers, and those who raised us, so that we may see your exalted Father and be filled with his divine nurture.
See, our Lord, that we have left our bodily wives and our earthly offspring, so that we may share in true union with you
and bear heavenly fruit from above, which no one can take away from us, but which will remain with us, and we with it.”
[The sixth act is finished.]
Seventh Act [Again, the seventh act.] While Judas was preaching throughout India, a commander of the king's army came to him and said, “I ask
you, servant of God—and you see that I have come to you in person, as to an apostle of God sent to heal people
who need the help given to them through your hands. I have heard about you that you take no payment from anyone,
but provide for those in need. For if you accepted payment, I would have sent you a large amount of silver and would not have come here myself.
For the king did nothing without [?]. I have abundant possessions, and I am rich and prominent throughout India. I have wronged no one.
Yet, contrary to this, this thing has happened to me. I have a wife, and I had a daughter [?] by her. I love her very much, as nature itself teaches.
And I have known no other woman besides her. Now it happened that there was a wedding feast in our city, and those holding it were very dear to me.
I also [?] sent many members of my household with her, and I adorned her and her daughter with many ornaments.
When it was time to leave, I sent torches and lamps after her. I myself was standing in the road, watching
for her to come, so that I could see her and welcome both her and her daughter with her. While I was standing there, I heard the sound of wailing and weeping.
“Alas for her! Alas for her!” came to my ears from every mouth. Then my servants came to me with their clothes torn.
They told me what had happened, saying to me, “We saw a man, and another, a youth, with him who looked like him. The man laid his hand on your wife, and the youth on your daughter.
The women recoiled from them, and we struck at them with swords, but our swords lodged in the ground.
At that very moment these women fell down. They were grinding their teeth and banging their heads against the ground.
So we came to tell you what happened.” When I heard these things from the members of my household, I tore my clothes and beat my face with my hands.
I ran through the street like a madman. I went and found them lying in the street, picked them up, and brought them to my house.
After a long time they regained consciousness. I made them comfortable and seated them, and I began asking my wife, “What happened to you?”
She said to me, “Do you not know what you have done to me? I asked you not to make me go to the wedding feast, because I was not feeling physically well.
As I was going along the road and reached a water channel that was pouring out water, I saw a black man
standing opposite me and shaking his head at me threateningly. Another, a youth who looked like him, was standing beside him. I said to my daughter, ‘Look at those people! How ugly they are!’
And my daughter said to me, ‘Those people—how ugly they are!’ And my daughter said to me, ‘I saw that youth whose teeth are like milk
and whose lips are like soot.’ We left them beside that water channel and went on. When evening came and we left the house where the wedding feast was being held,
we were coming back with the young servants and reached that water channel. My daughter saw them first.
She came and clung to me. After her, I too saw them coming toward us, and the young servants who were accompanying me ran away.
They struck me and my daughter and threw me down.” While she was telling me this, they came upon them.
They threw them down again. From that moment on, they have no longer been able to go out into the street, or even to go to the bathhouse,
or to a wedding feast, or to a house of mourning. Instead, they suffer night and day, the mother together with her daughter. They remain shut away in my house, in one room inside another,
because I have become a laughingstock through them, and because whenever those beings come upon them, they throw them down and expose them wherever they find them.
So I ask you and beg you: help me and have mercy on me. For three years now, no table has been set in my house with my wife and daughter at it
They have no rest [?], especially that poor daughter of mine, who has experienced nothing good.” When the apostle heard these things from [?] that commander,
he felt very sorry for him and said to him, “If you believe in my Lord Jesus Christ, who heals them, you will see them restored to health.”
When that commander heard this, he said to him—because he thought that he was Jesus—“I believe that you will heal them.”
The apostle said to him, “I am not Jesus, but his servant and apostle. Entrust yourself to him, and he will heal them
and help them.” That commander said to him, “Show me how to ask him and believe in him.”
The apostle said to him, “Direct your mind upward as far as you can, because he cannot now be seen with these bodily eyes.
But through faith he is known by his deeds and glorified for his acts of healing.” That commander raised his voice and said,
“I believe in you, Jesus Christ, God, because you are the Living One, the Son of the Living One. You became human and appeared as a physician, a giver of life, and a savior
to all those who truly turn to you. Yes, my Lord, I ask you and plead before you:
help my little faith and my distress, for I have taken refuge in you.” The apostle instructed Xanthippus, his deacon, to gather
all the brothers there. When he had gathered them all, the apostle came and stood among them and said to them,
“My children, my brothers and sisters in my Lord Jesus, remain in this faith and put your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ,
who has been proclaimed to you. Let your hope be directed toward him, and he will protect you. Do not turn away from him, because he will not abandon you.
Even if you sleep this sleep, in which a person who sleeps is unaware, he does not sleep.
Rather, he stays awake and protects you. And if you board a ship at sea, where none of you can help another,
he walks upon the waves of the sea and supports your ship. For I am now leaving you,
and I do not know whether I will see you again in the flesh. So do not be like the people of Israel,
