I will receive compensation, since I did you no wrong, yet you caused me suffering; I did not sin against you, yet you sinned against me. But even here, although I can take revenge on you
and do to you everything you did to me, listen to me instead, and come with me to my house. Speak to Mygdonia and persuade her to be with me
as she used to be. [?] she may see your face.” Judas went along with him, laughing, and said to him, “If human
beings loved God as they love their companions, he would give them everything they asked of him, and there would be nothing he would withhold from them.”
As he was saying these things, Judas entered Charisius’s house and found Mygdonia sitting, with Narcia standing in front of her,
her hands resting on her cheeks. She said to her nurse, “Mother, let the days pass quickly for me,
and let all the hours become a single hour, so that I may leave this world and go and see that beautiful one whose fame I have heard,
the one who lives and gives life to those who believe in him, where there is neither day nor night, and no darkness, but only light;
where there is neither good nor evil, neither rich nor poor, neither male nor female, neither slaves nor free people,
nor people of high standing who exalt themselves over the lowly.” While she was saying these things, Judas entered. She sprang up, stood, and bowed down before him.
Charisius said to him, “See how she fears you and loves you. Whatever you tell her, she does as you wish.” Judas said to her,
“My daughter Mygdonia, agree to what your brother Charisius tells you.” Mygdonia said to him, “You could not even speak of the deed;
how can you urge me to do it myself? For I heard you saying that this temporary life
is borrowed, that this comfort is temporary, and that these possessions do not last. You also used to say that whoever hates this life
goes on to receive eternal life, and whoever hates this light of day and night goes on to receive light in which there is no night.
You also used to say that everyone who leaves these earthly possessions goes on to find possessions that last forever, and other things.
Is it because you have become afraid that you say these things to me? Who does a deed and boasts about it, then turns around and denies it? And who builds a tower,
then turns around and tears it up from its foundations? Who digs a spring in a thirsty land, then throws stones into it and fills it up?
And who finds a valuable treasure and does not make use of it?” When Charisius, a relative of King Misdaeus, heard these things, he said,
“I will not be like them, and I will not rush to do you harm. But you I will bind,
because I have authority over you. I will not let you go to him and speak with him, with this sorcerer. If you agree—
and if not, I know what I will do.” Judas left Charisius’s house and went to the house of Siphor, the commander,
and stayed there. Siphor said to Judas, “Prepare a hall for yourself, and teach in it.” He did as he told him. And Siphor said to him,
Commander, my daughter, my wife, and I now live in holiness, with one mind and one love.
We ask to receive the seal from your hands and to become true servants of our Lord,
and to be counted among his sheep and his ewes.” Judas said, “I am thinking about speaking, but I am afraid.
I know that I cannot express what I know.” Then he began to speak about baptism, saying:
“This is baptism for the forgiveness of sins. This gives birth to new people. This renews minds and unites soul and body,
and establishes the new person in the Trinity. You are communion in the forgiveness of sins. Glory to you, hidden power of baptism!
Glory to you, hidden power that shares with us in baptism! Glory to you, power through which those who approach baptism in love are renewed.”
After saying these things, he poured oil on their heads and said, “Glory to you, beloved fruit! Glory to you, name of Christ!
Glory to you, hidden power that dwells in Christ!” As he spoke, they brought a large basin, and he baptized them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
When they had been baptized and dressed, he brought bread and wine, placed them on the table, and began to pronounce a blessing
over it, saying, “Living bread, whose eaters do not die! Bread that fills hungry souls with its goodness!
You who have been found worthy to receive the gift and to be for the forgiveness of sins, so that those who eat you may not die: we invoke the Father's name over you.
We invoke the Son's name over you. We invoke the Spirit's name over you, the exalted name hidden from everyone.” And he said, “In your name, Jesus,
may the power of blessing and thanksgiving come and rest upon this bread, so that all the souls that partake of it may be renewed
and their sins forgiven.” He broke it and gave it to Siphor, his wife, and his daughter. Now King Misdaeus, after releasing Judas Thomas,
went home to dine. He told his wife what had happened to his relative Charisius and said to her,
“Look, my sister, at what has happened to that wretched man. You know, my sister Tertia, that a man has no one like his wife, in whom he finds comfort.
It happened that Mygdonia went to see that sorcerer, whose reputation and deeds she had heard about. How he bewitched her and separated her from her husband, I do not know.
He does not know what to do. I wanted to destroy the man, but he would not let me. But you go and advise her to obey her husband
and not listen to that man's empty words.” In the morning Tertia got up and went to the house of Charisius, her husband's relative.
She found Mygdonia sitting on the ground, wearing sackcloth and ashes, asking her Lord to forgive her former sins
and to let her soon be delivered from the world. When Tertia came in to her, she said to Mygdonia, “My sister, my dear friend, my daughter, answer me.
What is this madness that has seized you? Why have you acted like a madwoman? Remember who you are; remember your lineage.
Consider your many relatives, and have pity on your true companion, Charisius. Do not do anything unworthy of your noble status.”
Mygdonia said to Tertia, “You have not heard the news of the new life, nor have you tasted the sound of the words of the herald of life.”
And you have not been delivered from the torments of corruption. Eternal life is not visible to you, and here you stand in this temporary life.
You have not experienced fellowship with the truth, and here you are tormented in the fellowship [?] of corruption. You wear clothes that wear out, and you do not long for everlasting clothes.
You are proud of this perishable beauty of yours, but you have no concern for the ugliness of your soul. Here you are, proud of your many slaves, yet your own soul from slavery
you have not freed. You are proud of the praise of many people, but you cannot escape judgment and death.” When Tertia heard these things from Mygdonia,
she quickly went to the house of Siphor, the commander, to see the new apostle who had come there. When she entered his presence,
he began to say to her, “Why have you come to see a man who, in the whole country, is [?], and is more despised and wretched than anyone else?
He has neither possessions nor wealth. Yet he has a possession that kings and rulers cannot take away from him,
and it neither perishes nor is plundered: Jesus Christ, the giver of life to all humanity, the Son of the living God,
who gives life to all who believe and come to his refuge and are numbered among his sheep.”
When Tertia heard these things from him, she said to him, “I too will be a participant and a servant in this life that you teach.
I too will become a member of the household of this God whom you proclaim, and I will receive from him this life which you promise
he gives to those who come to his refuge.” Judas said to her, “The treasury of the heavenly King is open, and everyone who is worthy receives and finds rest.
And when that person has found rest, they reign. But first, no one may approach him while unclean, or while their deeds are evil, for he knows what is in hearts
and in the mind, and no one deceives him. So you too, if you truly believe in him, he will make you worthy of his holy mysteries.
He will exalt you, enrich you, renew your mind, and make you an heir in his kingdom.” When Tertia heard these things,
she went home rejoicing. She found her husband Misdaeus waiting for her; he had not yet reclined to eat. He said to her,
“Why is your return from the street more pleasing to me today than on any other day? And why were you coming on foot, something women like you are not permitted to do?”
Tertia said to Misdaeus, “I owe you thanks for sending me to Mygdonia. I went and heard about a new life,
and I saw the new apostle of God. I believed that he is the apostle of God, who gives life to everyone who believes in him and does his will.
I too ought to repay you for the kindness you have shown me, and give you good advice, so that you too may become a king and a great man in heaven,
if you listen to me and do what I tell you. I urge you to fear God, who has come here through this stranger,
to fear God, who has come here through this stranger, and to keep yourself pure for God.
For this kingdom of yours is passing away, and this ease of yours will turn into distress. But come, go to that man, believe in him, and you will live forever.” And when
he heard these things from his wife Tertia, he struck his face with his hands, tore his clothes, and said,
“May the soul of Charisius have no rest, for he has brought distress upon my soul! May he have no hope, for he has cut off my own hope!”
He went along trembling, and in the street he found Charisius, his relative, and said to him, “Why have you taken me along as your companion to Sheol?
Why have you caused me loss when you have gained nothing? Why have you harmed me when you have received no benefit? Why have you killed me when you have not gained life?
Why have you wronged me when you have not become righteous? Why did you not let me destroy that sorcerer
before he corrupted my wife with his sorcery?” He was arguing with Charisius. Charisius said to Misdaeus,
“What has happened?” Misdaeus said to Charisius, “He has bewitched Tertia too.” They both went to the house of Siphor, the commander.
They found Judas sitting and teaching. All the people sprang up and stood, but Judas did not rise before them.
King Misdaeus realized that he was the one sitting there. He seized the chair, overturned it, and lifted it with both hands.

He struck him on the head with it and wounded him. He seized him, handed him over to his soldiers, and said to them, “Drag him away, so that I may sit in judgment and give him a hearing before everyone.”
They dragged Judas along until they reached the place where Misdaeus held court. When he reached that place,
he stood there, held by Misdaeus’s soldiers. Vizan, the son of King Misdaeus, came and said to the soldiers, “Hand him over to me so that I can speak with him until the king comes.”
They handed him over to him. He took Judas and went inside, to where the king sat to judge. Vizan said to him,
“You know that I am the son of King Misdaeus, and I have the authority to say whatever I want to the king. If I tell the king, he will strike you,
and if I tell him, he will kill you. Now tell me who your God is, and whose power you rely on and boast about.
If it is the craft of sorcerers, teach it to me, and I will speak to the king, and he will release you.” Judas said to Vizan,
“You are the son of Misdaeus, this king who passes away, but I am the servant of Jesus, the King who remains forever.
You have the authority to speak to your father and keep whomever you wish alive in this short life,
in which people do not remain, not even when you have granted it to them. Both you and your father will die.
But I ask my Lord and plead with him on behalf of people, and he gives them new life that lasts forever.
You boast about possessions [?], slaves, property, clothing, soldiers, couches, and food that passes away,
and an unclean bed. But I boast about poverty, self-denial, and lowliness,
fasting, prayer, abundant thanksgiving, fellowship with the brothers of the Holy Spirit, and conversation with the brothers whom God considers worthy to live forever.
You take refuge in a human being like yourself, who cannot even save himself from judgment and death. But I take refuge
in the one who condemns and acquits, who is great, and who is the judge of everyone. You and the one in whom you take refuge,
in the one who condemns and acquits, who is great, and who is the judge of everyone. You and the one in whom you take refuge,
exist today and tomorrow, but after a time you will no longer exist. But I take refuge in the one who exists forever.
And he knows all times and seasons. So you too, my son, if you wish to become a servant of this God whom I serve,
I can make you his quickly. And you will show yourself to be his servant through these things that I tell you: through holiness, the chief of all good things,
and the great beginning and seat of virtue, and fellowship with this God whom I proclaim; and through purity and humility,
and love and faith and hope in him, and the simplicity of a pure way of life.” Now the young man Vizan
had been persuaded through our Lord, and he was looking for an opportunity to have Judas released. While he was considering this, the king arrived.
The soldiers came, took Judas, and brought him outside. Vizan also went out with him and stood beside him.
The king sat down and sent for Judas to be brought in, with his hands bound behind his back. When he stood before him,
the king said to him, “Tell me who you are, and by whose power you do these things.” Judas said to him, “I am a human being like you,
and I do these things by the power of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” Mazdai said to him, “Tell the truth, before I destroy you.”
Judas said to him, “You do not have authority over me as you suppose, nor can you hurt me.” When Judas said these things, King Mazdai became angry.
He ordered iron plates to be heated and Judas to be made to stand barefoot on them. When they had set him down, he pulled off and removed his sandals.
He laughed and said, “Your wisdom, Jesus, is more excellent than all the wisdom of all human beings.
You take thought for them, and in your kindness prepare to meet these people's fury.” They brought the plates, which looked like fire.
They seized Judas to make him step onto them. Suddenly a great quantity of water rose from the ground.
The plates sank, and the men let go of him and fled. When the king saw the great quantity of water, he said to Judas,
“Ask your God to rescue us from this deadly flood, so that we do not die like this.” Judas prayed and said,
“Our Lord Jesus, I ask you: restrain this element and confine it to one place. You are the one who divided it
among many places and performed many wonders through your servant and apostle Judas. You who make my soul long to receive your radiance again,
who reward all my labors, who bring my soul to rest in its own nature, without admixture with what gives it form [?],
be the source of my life at all times. Still this flood yourself, so that it does not rise up and cause destruction.
For among those standing here are some who believe in you and live.” When Judas prayed, there was calm.
Little by little that water was swallowed up and could no longer be found. Instead, the place became dry, just as it had been.
When King Mazdai saw this, he said, “Take him away to prison while we consider what to do with him.”
Judas went to be imprisoned, and all the people followed him. Vizan, the son of King Mazdai, walked on Judas's right,
and Siphor, the commander, on his left. When Judas entered the prison, he gave permission to Siphor and Vizan.
and Siphor’s wife and daughter, so that they might sit down. For this reason they had come in with him: to hear the word of life.
For they knew that King Misdaeus would put him to death because of his great anger. And Judas began to say:
“You who free my soul from slavery to many, because I gave myself to be sold to one! And now, look, I am glad and rejoice.
For I know that the times and seasons, the years and months and days, have come to an end. And I will come and receive you, you who give me rest.
Look, I am being delivered from today and tomorrow, though it is today that concerns me. Look, I am leaving hope behind and receiving reality.
Look, I am escaping from everyday sorrow and joy, and clothing myself in joy alone. Look, I am becoming free from care, sorrow, and distress.
And I am dwelling in everlasting rest. Look, I am being freed from slavery, and I am going to the freedom to which I was called.
Look, I have served times and seasons, and I have been raised above times and seasons. Look, I am receiving [?] my reward from the Lord of rewards, who gives without withholding.
For his wealth is sufficient for all his gifts. Look, I am taking off my clothing and putting on clothing, and I will never take it off again. Look, I am lying down to sleep and rising,
and I will never die again. Look, they rejoice and look toward me, so that I may go and join in their joy and place flowers in their crowns.
Look, I am reigning in your kingdom, Jesus, for which I hoped while here. The wicked who hoped to enslave me under their authority are put to shame.
Look, the rebels are overthrown before me, for I have become greater than they are. Look, peace has come to the one at whom the powerful take aim.”
While Judas was saying these things, all those who were there were listening, and they thought
that his departure from the world would take place that very hour. And Judas said again, “Believe in the physician of all ailments, hidden and visible,
and the giver of life to souls that seek help from him. This is the freeborn man and the king’s son who became a slave and a poor man.
This is the physician of his creation, yet afflicted by his servants. This is the purifier of those who believe in him, yet despised and insulted by those who have not listened to him.
He frees those who belong to him from slavery, corruption, subjection, and loss, yet he is subjected to slavery and insulted by his servants.

This is the Father on high, the Lord of created things, and the judge of the world. This is the one who came from on high and appeared through the Virgin Mary, and is called the son of Joseph the carpenter.
This is the one whose bodily lowliness we saw with our eyes, and whose greatness we accepted by faith. This is the one whose holy body we touched with our hands,
and whose disfigured appearance we saw with our eyes, yet whose divine form we could not behold when we were alone on the mountain. This is the one who was called a deceiver,
yet he is the truthful one who does not lie, and he paid taxes and the poll tax for us and for himself. This is the one whom the enemy saw and became afraid; he was alarmed and questioned him

about who he was and what his standing was, but did not establish him in the truth, because there is no truth in him. This one, although he is Lord of the world, its desirable things, its possessions,
and all its comforts, himself removed them from it. And he warned those who listen to him and believe in him not to make use of these things.”
When he had finished saying these things, he stood up to pray and spoke as follows: “Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your kingdom come.
And may your will be done on earth as in heaven. Give us the constant bread of the day, and forgive us our debts and our sins.
so that we too may forgive our debtors. And do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one. My Lord and my God and my hope,
and my confidence, my teacher and my encourager, you are the one who taught us to pray like this. Look, I am praying your prayer,
and I am carrying out your will. Be with me until the end. You are the one who sowed life in me from childhood and protected me from corruption.
You are the one who brought me into the poverty of the world and invited me to your true riches. You are the one who made me know that I belong to you, and I have not approached a woman,
so that what is required for you might not be found defiled. My mouth is not sufficient to thank you, nor my mind to praise your grace toward me.
When I wanted to acquire possessions and become rich, you showed me in your vision that ruin had come to many
from wealth and possessions. I believed your vision and remained in poverty forever, until you,
the true riches, appeared to me. And those who are worthy of you, you have filled with your true riches.
And you have delivered us from need, worry, and greed. Look, now I have fulfilled your will and completed your work.
I have been poor, needy, a stranger, a slave, despised, imprisoned, hungry, thirsty, and naked,
and barefoot and weary for your sake. Let my confidence not cease, and let my hope in you not be put to shame. Let my labors not be empty,
and let my exertions not prove useless. Let my fasts and my continual prayers not perish, and let my deeds done in you not be changed.
Let the enemy not snatch your wheat seed from your land, and let his weeds not be found in it. For your land does not accept his weeds,
nor can they enter your farmer’s storehouses. And again he said: I planted your vine in the earth. May it send roots down into the depths
and extend its branches toward heaven. May its fruit be seen on earth, and may those who are unworthy, whom you have acquired, enjoy it.
The money you gave me I have placed on your table. Collect it and give it to me with its interest, as you promised. With your mina I have gained ten by trading.
May more be added to what I have, as you promised. I have forgiven my debtors their minas. Let what I forgave a debtor not be demanded from me. To supper
I was invited, and I came quickly. I excused myself from the village, the plow, and a wife. May I not reject it, and may I not taste it with oaths.
I was invited to the banquet and put on white clothes. May I be worthy of it. May my hands and feet not be bound, and may I not go out into the outer darkness.
My lamp is bright with its light. Preserve it, its Lord, until you leave the wedding feast and I meet you. May I not show it to you with its oil [?].
May my eyes [?] you, and may my heart rejoice that I have fulfilled your will and carried out your commandments. May I resemble the wise, God-fearing servant
who is not negligent in his vigilant diligence. I have labored in keeping watch all night, to guard my house against robbers so that it will not be broken into.
My waist is girded with truth, and my shoes are tight on my feet. May I not see their straps coming loose.
I put my hand to the blade of my plow and did not turn back, so that my furrows would not become crooked. My fields are white and already ripe for harvest.
May I receive my reward, the garment that never wears out. I have completed the labor that brings rest. I have kept my first watch.
And a second and a third time. I will meet you face to face and bow before your holy splendor. I have uprooted the house of my cages and demolished them to the ground.
I will draw from your inexhaustible treasure. I have dried up the moist spring within me. I will lean upon your living spring and rest upon it.
I have killed the prisoner whom you entrusted to me. Save the one within me who is free, and do not let my soul be deprived of its hope. The inner person
I have made outward, and the outward inward. May your will be fulfilled in all my limbs. I have not turned backward, but have stretched entirely forward. I will not display a wonder or a sign.
I have not raised the dead, nor have I killed the living. I have supplied what was lacking. May the ruler of both worlds receive the crown of victory.
I have suffered disgrace on earth; reward me in heaven. Let the powers not notice me, and let the authorities not plot against me.
Let the toll collectors not see me, and let the tax collectors not quarrel with me. Let the lowly not mock me, nor the wicked mock the diligent and humble one.
The slave, the despised, and the great one who exalts himself do not dare stand before me, because of your victorious power, Jesus, which surrounds me. For they flee and hide from it,
because they cannot look upon it. For they fall deceitfully and silently upon those who obey them.
Look, the portion of my children cries out and flashes, and no one hides from them, because it is the scent of their nature. The evil ones distinguish human beings.
The tree whose fruit is gall. I will pass quietly through their place and come to you.
May joy and peace support me, and may I stand before your glory. Let the accuser not look upon me.
Instead, let his eyes be blinded by your light, in which I [?]. Let his lying mouth be shut, for he has nothing against me. And he began again to speak to those who were
with him in prison: “Believe, my children, in this God whom I proclaim. Believe in Jesus Christ, whose good news I announce.
Believe in the one who gives life to his servants and helps them. Believe in the one who gives life to those who have labored in his service,
in this one in whom my soul now rejoices, because the time has come for me to go and meet him. Believe in this beautiful one,
whose beauty draws me to say something about what he is, although I am unable to describe him.
For you, my Lord, are the provision for my poverty, the one who supplies what I lack and provides for my need.
Be with me until the end, for I am coming to meet you.” Now that young man, Vizan, the son of King Mazdai,
was entreating him and saying to him, “I beg you, holy man, apostle of God, allow me to go and persuade the prison guards
and obtain [?] for me, so that you may go with me to my house and give me the seal of life [?]. Then I too will become a servant of this new God whom you proclaim.
For in my youth I conducted myself according to all these things you have spoken of, before my father Mazdai compelled me and gave me Mnesara as a wife.
For today I am twenty-[?] years old, and it has now been seven years since I was joined in marriage to a woman.
Before I took a wife, I had not known another woman, and in my father’s eyes I was considered an idle man
by him. I have not yet had a son or a daughter by the wife he gave me. My wife too has lived chastely with me throughout these years.”
And today, if she were well and saw you or heard your words, I would have relief, and she would live.
And she would receive eternal life. For she has been in great distress for a long time now,
because of her illness. So I will plead with the keeper of the prisoners, if you promise me that you will go with me to my house, for I live by myself, alone in the courtyard,
and heal the sick woman who is ill.” When Judas, the apostle of the Most High, heard these things, the apostle said to Iuzanes:
“My son, if you believe, you will see the wonders of our God, how he gives life and shows mercy to his servants.”
While they were speaking, Tertia, Mygdonia, and her nurse Narcia were standing at the prison gate.
They gave the prison guards three hundred and sixty silver coins, and the guards brought them in to Judas.
They entered and saw Judas, Siphor, Iuzanes, Siphor’s wife and daughter, and all the prisoners sitting and listening to Judas.
The three women stood before him, and he said to them, “Who let you come to us? And who opened for you the gate that had been sealed

against you?” Tertia said to him, “Was it not you who opened the gate for us and told us to come to the prison, so that we might go and bring our brothers who are there, and then our Lord would show his glory among us?
When we reached the gate, you disappeared from us, and we heard the sound of the gate closing in our faces. But we gave the guards their payment and came in.
And here we stand, asking you to grant our wish and let us help you escape until King Mazdai’s anger against you subsides.”
Judas said to Tertia, “First tell us how you were imprisoned.” Tertia said to him, “You yourself have been away from us
for only an hour, and do you not know how we were imprisoned? But if you wish to hear, listen.
King Mazdai sent for me and had me brought—I, Tertia myself—and said to me, ‘That sorcerer does not yet have power over you.
For I have heard that he works sorcery with Christ, water, bread, and wine, and he has not yet bewitched you.
So obey what I tell you, so that I do not torture you until I destroy you. For I know
that as long as he has not given you water, oil, bread, and wine, he has not yet gained complete power over you.’ But I said to him, ‘Do whatever you wish to me.
You have power over my body, to do whatever you wish to it, but I will not destroy my soul along with you.’
When he heard this from me, he imprisoned me in a dark room beneath his dining hall. His relative Charisius also brought Mygdonia and Narcia
and imprisoned them beside me. The light did not leave us. And you yourself brought us out, and here we stand before you. But give us the seal,
so that Mazdai’s hope concerning me may be cut off, for he has these intentions toward me.” When Judas, the apostle of our Lord, heard these things that she said, he said:
“Praise to you, Jesus of many forms! Praise to you, who appear in the likeness of our lowly humanity! Glory to you, who strengthen us, encourage us, establish us, and make us glad,
who stand beside us in all our afflictions, strengthen our weakness, and give courage to our fear.” When he had said these things,
the prisoners took courage. And the guards said, “Blow out the lamps, so that no one accuses us before King Mazdai.”
They blew out all the lamps and went to sleep. But Judas said to our Lord, “Now it is for you to act swiftly.
Jesus, our illuminator, see how the children of darkness have darkened us with their darkness. But you, our Lord, enlighten me with the light of your nature.”
Suddenly the whole prison became as bright as daylight. Everyone imprisoned there was asleep.
Only those who believed in our Lord were awake. Judas said to Vizan, “Go ahead of us and prepare what we need for our service.” Vizan said to him,
“Who will open the prison doors for us? They have locked them all, and the guards are asleep.” Judas said to him,
“Believe in Jesus and do not doubt. Go, and you will find the doors standing open on their hinges.”
He went out and walked ahead of them, while all the others followed Judas. When they were halfway along the road,
Mnesara, Vizan’s wife, met them as she was coming to the prison. She recognized him and said to him, “My brother Vizan!”
He said to her, “Yes! And are you my sister Mnesara?” She said to him, “Yes.” He said to her, “Where are you going alone at this hour?
And how were you able to get out of bed?” She said to him, “This young man laid his hand on me, and I was healed.
I saw in my dream that I should go to that stranger where he is imprisoned, so that I might be completely healed.” Vizan said to her,
“Which young man is with you?” She said to him, “Do you not see him? Look, he is holding my right hand and supporting me.” While they were speaking,
Judas arrived with Siphor, his wife and daughter, and with Mygdonia, Tertia, and Narcia. They came and entered Vizan’s house.
When Mnesara, Vizan’s wife, saw him—when Mnesara, Vizan’s wife, saw him, she bowed down and prostrated herself before him, saying, “You have come, my healer from this painful illness!
You are the one I saw in my dream, who entrusted this young man to me to bring me to you in the prison. Your kindness did not allow you
to let me grow weary; instead, you came to me.” When she had said this, she turned around, but the young man was not there.
She said to Judas, “I cannot walk by myself, and the young man you entrusted to me is not here.” Judas said to her,
“From now on, Jesus will be your support.” She ran and went ahead of them. When they entered the house of Vizan, the son of King Mazdai,
it was nighttime, and our Lord gave them abundant light. Judas began to pray, saying,
“Companion [?] and strength of the weak, hope and confidence of the poor, refuge and rest of the weary, voice that came from on high,
who holds the hearts of those who believe in him, refuge and harbor of travelers in the land of darkness,
physician who heals freely among humankind, who was crucified for many, though no one was crucified for him: you are the one who descended to Sheol with mighty power.
The dead saw you and came to life, and the ruler of death could not endure it. You ascended in great glory [?],
and brought up with you all who took refuge in you. You opened a road for them to the heights, and all those you redeemed followed in your footsteps.
You brought them into your fold and mingled them with your sheep, Son of perfect mercy, who were sent to us in power from the Father.

Whose works praise him. The Son who was sent from the exalted and perfect Fatherhood. The Lord of possessions that cannot be defiled. The rich one who filled his creation from the treasury of his wealth.
The poor one who suffered need and hunger for forty days. The one who satisfies our thirsty souls with his goodness.
You, my Lord, be with Iuzanes, Tertia, and Mnesara. Gather them into your fold and include them among your own.
Be their guide on the road of error. Be their healer in the place of sickness. Be their strength in the place of weariness.
Sanctify them in the unclean place. Cleanse them from corruption in the enemy’s domain. Be a physician to their bodies and give life to their souls.
Make them holy shrines and temples, and let the Holy Spirit dwell in them. When he had prayed these things, he said to Mygdonia:
“My daughter, undress your sisters.” She undressed them, put loincloths on them, and brought them to him. Iuzanes, however, approached first.
Judas took oil, offered praise over it, and said, “Beautiful fruit, you who have been found worthy to boil through the word of sanctification,
so that people may clothe themselves in you and through you overcome their enemies, once they have been cleansed of their former deeds.
Yes, my Lord, come and rest upon this oil, just as you rested upon the wood, and those who crucified you could not endure your word.
Let your gift come, the gift you breathed upon your enemies, so that they drew back and fell on their faces.
Let it rest upon this oil, over which we invoke your name.” He poured it on Iuzanes’ head,
and then on the heads of the others, and said, “In your name, Jesus Christ, let it bring these souls forgiveness of debts
and sins, the defeat of the enemy, and healing for their souls and bodies.” He had instructed Mygdonia to anoint the women,
while he himself anointed Iuzanes. When he had anointed them, he brought them down into the water in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
When they had been baptized and had come up, he brought bread and a cup of mixed wine, pronounced a blessing over it, and said:
“We eat your holy body, which was crucified for us, and drink your life-giving blood, which was poured out for us.
May the body bring us life, and your blood forgiveness of sins. In return for the gall you drank for us, may the bitterness of our enemy be taken away from us.
In return for the vinegar you drank for us, may our weakness be strengthened. In return for the spittle you received for us, may we receive your perfect life.
Because you received a crown of thorns for us, may we receive from you a crown that does not wither. Because you were wrapped in linen for us,
may we be strengthened by your great, invincible power. Because you were buried in a new tomb in place of our death, may we too receive fellowship with you [?] in heaven.
Just as you rose, may we be raised and stand before you at the judgment of truth.” He broke the Eucharist and gave it to Iuzanes and Tertia,
to Mnesara, Siphor, and Mygdonia, and to Siphor’s wife and daughter. He said, “May this Eucharist bring you
life, rest, joy, health, and healing for your souls and bodies.” They said, “Amen.”
A voice was heard saying to them, “Yes and amen.” When they heard this voice, they fell on their faces. Again a voice was heard saying:
Do not be afraid. Only believe firmly. And Judas was going to be imprisoned, along with Tertia, Mygdonia, and Narcia.
They too were going to be imprisoned. Judas said to them, “My daughters and sisters in our Lord, my companions and servants of Jesus Christ,
listen to me on this last day, as I deliver my message to you. I will no longer speak with you in this world, but I am being raised up to my Lord Jesus Christ,
to the one who bought me, to the one who humbled his exalted self to my lowliness and brought me up to his greatness that never passes away.
He made me worthy to be his worker in truth and faithfulness. And now I rejoice that the time is complete and the day has arrived for me to go and receive my reward from my Lord.
For the Lord who rewards me is just, and he knows how he ought to repay me. He is neither wicked nor envious, but his gifts are abundant.
He gives without calculating, because he is confident that his possessions will not run out. Listen, my daughters: I am not Jesus, but I am Jesus’ servant. I am not
the Christ, but I am a servant [?] before him. I am not the Son of God, but I pray and ask
that I may be worthy of God. But you, my daughters, remain firm in faith in Jesus Christ, and await the hope of the Son of God.
Do not grow weary in affliction, my daughters, and do not doubt because you see me being mistreated and imprisoned again,
and dying. For I am fulfilling my Lord’s will. If I were to pray that I should not die, you know that I could do so.
But this thing you see is not death; it is release from the world. That is why I welcome it joyfully.
That is why I am being set free: to go and receive the one who is beautiful, the one whom I love,
the holy one. For I have labored greatly in his service, and I have finished because of his grace, which supported me and did not abandon me.
So do not let that enemy gain access to you through deceit, or cast doubt into your minds. Let there be no room for that deceiver and troublemaker.
For the one whom you have received and believed in is more fearsome than he. Await his coming, when he will come and receive you,
that is, when you will go and see him.” When Judas had finished speaking to them, he went inside the dark building.
Judas said, “You who give us life and have suffered many things for us, let these doors be as
they were, and let them be sealed with their seals.” He left the women and went himself to be imprisoned.
But they were distressed and wept, because they knew that King Mazdai would kill him.
When he went in to be imprisoned, he found the guards arguing and saying, “What wrong have we done to this sorcerer,
that he has opened the doors by his magical arts and wanted to let all these prisoners escape? Let us go and inform King Mazdai,
and tell him also about his wife and his son, who come to him.” While the chief jailer was saying these things,
Judas remained silent and listened. They rose early in the morning, went to King Mazdai, and said to him, “Our lord the king,
either take that sorcerer away or imprison him somewhere else, for we cannot guard him, because twice
“Your good fortune keeps the prisoners under guard. Otherwise, they would all have escaped. For we shut the doors and then find them open.”
“Even your wife and your son, along with the rest of the people, do not leave his side.” When King Mazdai heard these things,
he went to inspect the seals he had placed on the doors. He found the seals just as they had been, and said to the guards,
“Why are you lying? Look, the seals on the buildings remain intact. How can you say that Tertia and Mygdonia come to him in the
prison?” The guards said, “We have told you the truth.” Then King Mazdai went and sat in judgment.
He sent for Judas, had him brought in and stripped, and put a loincloth around his waist. They stood him before Mazdai, and Mazdai said to him,
“Are you a slave or a free man?” Judas said to him, “I am a slave, and you have no authority over me in anything.” Mazdai said to him,
“How did you escape and come to [?] country?” Judas said to him, “I came here to bring many to life through the word.
And through your hands I am leaving this world.” Mazdai said to him, “Who is your master? What is his name? And what country are you from?”
Judas said to him, “My master is your master and the master of the whole world, the Lord of heaven and earth.” Mazdai said to him, “What is his name?”
Judas said to him, “You cannot hear his true name now, at this time. But the name given to him is Jesus Christ.”
Mazdai said to him, “I have not hurried to destroy you, but have been patient with you. Yet you have added to your deeds.
Your sorceries have become known throughout the country. And I will [?] for you, so that they accompany you and go with you,
while our country is cleared of them.” Judas said to him, “These sorceries that you say
go along with me do not depart from here.” While he was saying these things,
Mazdai was considering how to order his death, because he was afraid of the large crowd gathered there.
For many had believed in our Lord, including some of the king’s officials. Mazdai rose, took Judas, and went outside the city.
A few armed soldiers went with him. The people thought that Mazdai wanted to learn something from him.
They stood watching him. When they had gone about half a mile, he handed him over to some of the soldiers who were with him
and to one of the officials. He said to them, “Go up this mountain and stab him.” Then he turned back to return to the city.
The people were running after Judas to rescue him. But the soldiers walked on his right and his left,
holding spears. The official held him by the hand and supported him.
Judas said, “Oh, the hidden mysteries that are fulfilled in me right up to my departure! Oh, the riches of his grace,
of him who does not let us feel bodily suffering! How they surround me with weapons and fight against me to the death!
And I am being handed over to one. For look, a great man leads me and holds me by the hand, to hand me over to the one I am awaiting.”
who received him. My Lord too [?], for he suffered from one man, at the hands of one man. And when he went up the mountain, to the place where they were to stab Judas,
he said to those who were holding him, “Listen to me, even now, for I stand at the point of departing from this world.
Do not let the eyes of your hearts become blind, or your ears become deaf, so that you too cannot hear. Believe in this God whom I proclaim.
Do not conduct yourselves according to the hardness of your hearts. Instead, conduct yourselves in every way that befits the freedom and glory of children
and life with God.” Judas said to Iuzanes, the son of Mazdai, the earthly king, and a servant of Jesus Christ,
“Allow those who serve the will of King Mazdai to have their way. I am going to pray.” And Iuzanes spoke to those soldiers,
and they allowed [?] to go. Judas went and prayed, saying this: “My Lord and my God, my hope and my Savior,
my guide and my companion in all the places where I have traveled in your name, be with all your servants.
Accompany me too, for I am coming to you. For I have entrusted my soul to you, and no one will take it from your hands.
Do not let my sins hinder me. Look, my Lord, I have fulfilled your will and become a slave for the sake of this freedom that I receive today. You, my Lord Jesus,
give it to me and bring it to completion with [?]. For I have no doubts at all about your truth and your love.
But I speak before you so that these people standing here may hear.” While Judas was praying these things, he said to those soldiers,
“Come, carry out the will of the one who sent you.” The soldiers came and struck him together, and he fell and died.
All the brothers wept together. They brought fine [?] and many linen cloths, and buried Judas
in the tomb where the former kings had been buried. Siphor and Iuzanes did not want to go down to the city.
Instead, they stayed there all day, and they also spent the night there. Judas appeared to them and said, “I am not here.
Why are you sitting here waiting for me? I have gone up to my Lord and received what I was waiting and hoping for.
But get up and go down from here. For in a little while you too will be gathered to me.” Now Mazdai and his relative Charisius
brought Mygdonia and Tertia and put great pressure on them, but they would not yield to their wishes.
Judas appeared to them and said, “My daughters, do not forget Jesus, our light, the Holy and Living One.
He will soon give you relief and help.” And when King Mazdai and his relative Charisius saw that they would not be persuaded
by them, they allowed them to live according to their own wishes. All the brothers there would gather together, pray, offer the offering, and break bread.
For Judas had appointed Siphor a priest and Iuzanes a deacon on the mountain when he was going to his death. Our Lord helped them in his love,
and through them he spread faith in him. After a long time, it happened that one of King Mazdai’s sons became possessed by a demon.
No one could bind him, because he was very violent. King Mazdai thought to himself and said:
“That I may go and open Judas’s tomb, take a bone [?] from the bones of God’s apostle, and hang it on my son, and he will be healed.”
Judas appeared to him in a vision and said to him, “You did not believe in the living; now you want to believe in the dead. But do not be afraid.
My Lord Christ will be gracious to you because of his kindness.” He could not find his bones, for one of the brothers had stolen them
and taken them to the West. But King Mazdai took some dust from the place where the apostle’s bones had lain
and hung it on his son, saying, “I believe in you now, my Lord Jesus, because he has left me—the one who constantly troubles
people so that they do not see the light.” When he hung it on his son and believed, his son was healed. He himself used to gather with the brothers.
King Mazdai would bow his head beneath the hand of Siphor the elder, pleading and asking all the brothers
to pray for him, so that he might receive mercy with them before our Lord Jesus Christ in his kingdom forever and ever. Amen.
The Acts of Judas Thomas, the apostle of my Lord Jesus Christ, are ended. He was martyred in the land of India at the hands of King Mazdai.
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and at all times and forever and ever. Amen.
